bullets.title: Jobs Friday: Consensus Expects ~88K Payrolls, 4.3% Unemployment
bullets.body: Street consensus heading into May payrolls expects 88,000 job gains, unemployment steady at 4.3%, labor participation flat at 61.8%, and average weekly hours at 34.3—characterized by one account as 'a number I would characterize as weak.'

bullets.title: Tech Futures Extend Global Selloff Pre-Payrolls: NDX -1.13%, S&P -0.6%
bullets.body: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1.13% and S&P 500 futures dropped 0.6% in overnight/pre-market action as the Asian session closed with KOSPI -6%, TAIEX -2%, and Nikkei -1%. Markets also tracking Korea won at 17-year lows vs. dollar (USD/KRW ~1,547).

bullets.title: NVIDIA Completes HBM4 Qualification From All Three Major Memory Makers
bullets.body: NVIDIA has secured HBM4 approval from all three major memory suppliers (SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung), a key milestone enabling the production ramp for next-gen AI systems.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang Korea Visit: R&D Center, Meetings With Samsung, SK, Hyundai; Robotics Pitch
bullets.body: Jensen Huang announced NVIDIA will open an R&D center in South Korea and confirmed meetings with Hyundai Motor Group, Samsung Electronics, and SK Group. Huang called robotics 'Korea's next key industry' and highlighted significant deployment opportunities in Korean industries.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang Hints at 'Upcoming Surprises'; AI Buildout Accelerating
bullets.body: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang hinted at upcoming product or partnership surprises (no specifics) and stated the global AI buildout is accelerating. NVIDIA's full-stack AI factory platform cited as the foundation for expanding AI clouds worldwide.

bullets.title: TSMC: 2030 Demand Visibility, Mid-30% Revenue Growth Target, Cautious on Pricing
bullets.body: TSMC Chairman C.C. Wei stated demand visibility extends to 2030—far beyond the typical few-quarter-to-one-year window—with mid-30% YoY revenue growth targeted this year. Wei warned against aggressive 'memory chip-style' pricing, prioritizing sustainable long-term operations. The AI demand surge 'caught even Jensen by surprise.'

bullets.title: TSMC: High-NA EUV in Research (Not Mass Production), CoPoS Pilot Line Operational
bullets.body: TSMC purchased ASML's High-NA EUV tools but is still optimizing for manufacturing cost efficiency—not yet in mass production. A CoPoS advanced packaging pilot line is already built with volume ramp expected in 2–3 years. CEO Wei reiterated TSMC will 'work relentlessly' to beat rivals including TeraFab.

bullets.title: SK Hynix: No New NAND Capacity; DRAM Targeting 2x Wafers by 2030–31; US Listing Gets 'Tremendously Positive' Response
bullets.body: SK Hynix confirmed no plans to add new NAND flash capacity (only YMTC and Kioxia expanding). The company is targeting roughly double current DRAM wafer production by 2030–31, per Jensen Huang's 'please make more' directive. Separately, SK Hynix's US listing plan is reportedly attracting 'tremendously positive' investor feedback.

bullets.title: BNP Cuts DRAM/NAND ASP Peak Forecast to Mid-2026; QoQ Declines Starting Early 2025
bullets.body: BNP Paribas analyst Karl Ackerman now expects DRAM and NAND ASP peaks by mid-2026 (vs. prior mid-2027 forecast), with quarter-over-quarter ASP declines commencing in early 2025. Recent AI-driven ASP surge is seen as pulling forward the cycle.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Rubin NVSwitch Tray BoM Open-Sourced; Embeds AMD EPYC CPUs (9 per VR200 Rack)
bullets.body: NVIDIA open-sourced its Rubin NVSwitch Tray bill of materials and diagram. Each tray uses an AMD EPYC 3151 embedded CPU—9 per VR200 rack—an overlooked AMD socket win inside NVIDIA's next-gen infrastructure.

bullets.title: Intel 18A Called 'Game Changer' Based on TEM Imagery; Multiple Fintwit Accounts Bullish
bullets.body: Multiple accounts cited TEM images of Intel's 18A nanosheet and power-via patterning as 'absolutely amazing,' calling the node a 'game changer.' The positive commentary appears based on process quality validation rather than yield or customer ramp news.

bullets.title: Foxconn May Revenue +39.6% YoY; AI Racks Driving Above-Seasonal Q2
bullets.body: Foxconn reported May revenue +39.57% year-over-year. While Q2 is traditionally a weak season for ICT, the company said AI rack momentum is sustaining growth above previously anticipated Q2 levels.

bullets.title: Broadcom $285B Market Cap Rout on Revenue Outlook Disappointment
bullets.body: Broadcom suffered a ~$285 billion market cap decline following a weaker-than-hoped AI revenue outlook. Despite this, broader S&P 500 and most megacap AI stocks finished the prior session higher, suggesting selective rather than systemic de-rating.

bullets.title: Marvell: Jensen Calls It 'Next Trillion-Dollar Company'; +187% Since Congressional Buy; MRVL AI Connectivity Thesis
bullets.body: Jensen Huang publicly labeled Marvell the 'next trillion-dollar company.' MRVL is up 187% since Rep. Byron Donalds (who sits on an AI subcommittee) purchased shares. Fintwit characterizes MRVL as the 'architect of the AI connectivity backbone' post its strategic semiconductor pivot.

bullets.title: CRWV and NBIS Flagged as Beneficiaries of Great American AI Act of 2026
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side desks are describing the Great American AI Act of 2026 (expected to formalize imminently) as a 'win-win' for CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) in AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: AAOI: Trader Averaging Up Since $28; 800G/1.6T Optical Transceiver Demand Cited
bullets.body: One fintwit account is steadily averaging up on AAOI since $28, citing high demand for 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers and the potential for the stock to double or triple on execution. Separately, the same account is bullish on CIEN, LITE, COHR, GLW, NOK in the photonics/optics complex.

bullets.title: Alphabet $84B Equity Raise Rated Credit Positive by Moody's; Palantir-Google Cloud Partnership
bullets.body: Moody's called Alphabet's $84B equity raise credit positive. Palantir announced a multi-tiered partnership with Google Cloud enabling integrations across Google services.

bullets.title: Tech Job Cuts at Highest Monthly Level Since Aug 2024; 123K YTD (+65% YoY)
bullets.body: US tech companies have announced 123,000+ job cuts YTD, up over 65% vs. the same period in 2025—the highest monthly pace since August 2024. 40% of recent layoffs broadly are being attributed to AI/automation by companies. GitHub commits meanwhile are up 600% but actual business productivity grew only 0.3% in Q1 2026.

bullets.title: S&P DJI Megacap Review Concludes: No Changes; SpaceX Excluded for 12+ Months
bullets.body: S&P Dow Jones Indices concluded its megacap methodology consultation with no changes to eligibility criteria. SpaceX, Anthropic, and similar mega-cap IPOs will not be added to the S&P 500/400/600 for at least 12 months post-listing. FTSE Russell and Nasdaq have faster inclusion timelines.

bullets.title: QQQ/Tech Showing Late-Cycle Bearish Divergence; VIX Timing Framework Highlighted
bullets.body: One fintwit account with a self-described strong track record warned that QQQ and tech are showing 'late-cycle movement patterns' with increasing bearish divergence at each marginal high and 'bulls becoming overextended and greedy.' Separately, VIX-based timing was highlighted: sell when VIX is low, buy when high.
